newsitem.title: USA: Cook County may pursue a 3rd refunding late in '97.
newsitem.headline: Cook County may pursue a 3rd refunding late in '97.

text.p: Cook County saved about $5.7 million through its sale of $206.4 million of general obligation refunding bonds this week and could go to market for another issuance of more than $200 million later this year, Chief Financial Officer Thomas Glaser said.
The issue on Wednesday was "well-received" through all maturities and some in the nine- to 13-year range were oversubscribed, Glaser said late Wednesday.

Cook County commissioners in February 1996 gave officials the authority to refund up to $554 million of bonds. About $120 million of general obligation refunding bonds were sold in July 1996, followed by a second refunding on Wednesday.
The county could go to the market to refund the remaining bonds this fall if conditions are favorable, Glaser said.
Cook County officials had planned to go to the market with a second refunding of up to $287 million of bonds in February when the market took an unfavorable turn, Glaser said.
The lead manager on the deal, Smith-Barney, notified the county on Friday that conditions were favorable for a portion of that deal and things moved quickly from there, Glaser said.
With the savings realized on Wednesday and those from the previous refunding, Cook County has already saved the $10 million it had sought for the entire refunding, Glaser noted.
